text: Intraset rest training has been proposed as a method for overcoming the negative effects of peripheral fatigue. As the name implies, the strategy involves resting for a prescribed period of time between repetitions within a given set. These intraset rest periods conceivably allow for the accumulation of a greater total training volume while maintaining high magnitudes of loading, which in turn may promote superior muscular adaptations. However, given the mechanistic role of metabolic stress in resistance training-induced hypertrophy (86), it is unclear whether potential benefits associated with intraset rest supersede the negative implications of altering fatigue levels.
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
